newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Fannie Mae A$ global bond aiding liquidity-SBCW.
newsitem.headline: Fannie Mae A$ global bond aiding liquidity-SBCW.

text.p: The largest ever Australian dollar global bond launched on Wednesday by Fannie Mae could be the start of a trend to fill the vacuum left by a lack of supply from Australian authorities.
"Liquidity is a key issue for investors in Australian dollar debt securities, said Sharon Mitchell, Head of Interest Rate Sales for SBC Warburg Australia.

"The shortage of government and semi-government securities means global issues of one billion dollars or more, supported by a strong underwriting group, will appeal to the international investors community," Mitchell said.
The A$1.0 billion offering, which matures on July 10, 2002, will be priced on Thursday at a spread of 19.5 basis points over the 9.75 percent March 2002 Australian government bond.
The proceeds of the issue are swapped back to U.S. dollars, SBC Warburg said in a statement.
SBC Warburg acted as bookrunner for the issue and was joint lead manager with Merrill Lynch International and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.

"Fannie Mae's high credit quality and strong name recogntion makes the issue attractive to investors seeking Australian dollar exposure and credit risk diversification," said Manfred Schepers, Global Head of rates Origination for SBC Warburg in London.
The AAA rated issue also marked the first U.S. agency global issue denominated in Australian dollars.

"We are delighted that investors in Asia, Europe and the U.S. have responded very enthusiastically to this first U.S. agency global Australian dollar offering. We look forward to the successful pricing of the bond on Thursday and strong secondary
performance thereafter," Mehmood Nathani, Director, Long Term Funding, for Fannie Mae.
The co-lead managers to the issue are BZW, CS First Boston, Daiwa Securities, Tordom and Westpac.
